examples.en: I had a high fever, so I bought suppositories at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 아기가 약을 못 먹으면 좌약을 쓰기도 해요.
examples.en: If a baby can't take medicine by mouth, a suppository is sometimes used.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 좌약 한 개를 처방해 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor prescribed me one suppository.
They told me to keep the suppositories in the fridge.

examples.ko: 좌약이 녹지 않게 시원한 곳에 보관하세요.
examples.en: Please store the suppositories in a cool place so they don't melt.

examples.ko: 먹는 약 대신 좌약으로 바꿨더니 편해졌어요.
examples.en: I switched from oral medicine to a suppository and it got easier.

explain: 알약이나 물약처럼 먹는 약이 아니라, 몸에 넣어서 쓰는 약이에요. 아이가 열이 나서 약을 삼키기 힘들 때처럼 병원이나 약국에서 이야기할 때 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike pills or syrups, this medicine is not swallowed but inserted into the body. You will hear it at hospitals and pharmacies, for example when a child has a fever and has trouble swallowing medicine.

examples.ko: 좌우간 먼저 가 보고 나서 이야기해요.
examples.en: Anyway, let's go and see first, then talk.
In any case, we have to finish by tomorrow.

examples.ko: 비가 오든 안 오든 좌우간 출발해요.
examples.en: Rain or shine, we leave anyway.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 뭐라고 하든 좌우간 나는 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Whatever he says, I'm going anyway.

examples.ko: 좌우간 일단 밥부터 먹고 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Anyway, let's eat first and think after.
I don't know the reason, but anyway, I'm glad.

explain: '어쨌든', '아무튼'과 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 앞 이야기가 어떻든 상관없이 중요한 말로 넘어갈 때 문장 맨 앞에 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '아무튼'이 더 흔해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '어쨌든' and '아무튼', so you can swap them. You usually put it at the start of a sentence to move on to the main point regardless of what came before. In daily talk '아무튼' is more common.

examples.en: Anyway, the exam is over, so get some good rest.
In any case, let's definitely meet this weekend.
Anyway, I'm really glad you're safe.
In any case, I'll take responsibility for that.
Either way, we have to decide today.

examples.ko: 좌우지간 한번 해 보고 안 되면 다시 생각해요.
examples.en: Anyway, let's try it once, and if it doesn't work, think again.

explain: '좌우간'과 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 말하는 사람이 '어쨌든 이게 중요해요'라고 마무리하거나 화제를 바꿀 때 써요. 더 흔한 말은 '아무튼', '어쨌든'이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '좌우간', so they are interchangeable. A speaker uses it to say 'what matters is this' or to change the topic. '아무튼' and '어쨌든' are more common.

examples.en: That department head was demoted to a regional branch.

examples.ko: 실수 한 번 때문에 좌천될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: One mistake could get you demoted.

examples.ko: 그는 본사에서 작은 사무소로 좌천돼서 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: He was sent from headquarters to a small office and had a hard time.
Even after being demoted, he kept working hard.
There's a rumor that he fought with the boss and got demoted.

examples.ko: 좌천되면 어떤 기분일지 상상도 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't even imagine how it feels to be demoted.

explain: '승진하다'의 반대로, 지위가 낮아지거나 중요하지 않은 곳으로 밀려날 때 써요. 단순한 '전근'과 달리 벌이나 불이익이라는 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 '밀려나다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '승진하다' (to be promoted) and is used when someone's rank drops or they are pushed to a less important place. Unlike a plain transfer, it carries a feeling of punishment or disadvantage. In daily talk people also say '밀려나다'.

examples.en: Thick rain pours down on the window.
When I turned on the tap, water gushed out.
The shower is pouring so hard that an umbrella is useless.
I sprayed water all over the yard with a hose.

examples.ko: 밤새 비가 좍좍 내려서 잠을 설쳤어요.
examples.en: It poured all night, so I slept badly.

examples.ko: 큰 물통을 기울이자 물이 좍좍 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: When I tilted the big water jug, water poured out.

explain: 비나 물이 세게 쏟아지는 모양과 소리를 나타내요. '주룩주룩'보다 기세가 센 느낌이라 소나기나 수돗물처럼 많이 쏟아질 때 잘 어울려요. 보통 '내리다, 쏟아지다, 뿌리다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes water or rain pouring hard, along with the sound. It feels stronger than '주룩주룩', so it fits downpours and rushing tap water. It usually goes with '내리다', '쏟아지다' and '뿌리다'.

examples.en: Water is flowing out of the tap.
That child recites the multiplication table fluently.

examples.ko: 동생이 영어 책을 좔좔 읽어서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that my younger sibling read the English book so fluently.
The stream flows along with a rushing sound.

examples.ko: 발표 내용을 좔좔 말하는 친구가 부러워요.
examples.en: I envy my friend who can speak the presentation so smoothly.
Rainwater poured off the roof.

explain: 물이 힘차게 흐르는 모양에서, 막힘없이 줄줄 읽거나 외우는 모습으로도 넓게 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 '아주 유창하다'는 칭찬 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '줄줄'이 있어요.
explain_en: From water flowing strongly, it is also used for reading or reciting without stumbling. Said about a person, it sounds like praise for being very fluent. A similar word is '줄줄'.

examples.en: The suspect's charge was announced on the news.
Let's check the charge first and then talk.
They say his charge is fraud.

examples.ko: 죄명에 따라 형량이 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: The sentence can differ depending on the charge.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 억울한 죄명을 쓰고 감옥에 갔어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie went to prison under an unjust charge.
The charge was written wrongly in the document.

explain: 사기, 절도처럼 어떤 죄인지 부르는 법적인 이름이에요. 아직 확정되지 않은 의심을 말할 때는 '혐의'를 쓰고, 뒤에 오는 말로는 '형량'이 자주 나와요. 주로 뉴스나 재판 이야기에서 들어요.
explain_en: It is the legal name of a crime, such as fraud or theft. For suspicion that is not yet confirmed, people say '혐의', and '형량' (sentence) often comes next. You mostly hear it in news and trial stories.

examples.en: In the movie, the main character appeared in a prisoner uniform.

examples.ko: 죄수복이 몸에 안 맞아서 불편해 보였어요.
examples.en: The prisoner uniform didn't fit, so he looked uncomfortable.
I dressed up as a prisoner at the Halloween party.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 죄수복 차림으로 법정에 섰어요.
examples.en: That actor stood in court wearing a prisoner uniform.
A picture of him changed into a prisoner uniform was on the news.
You're wearing a striped outfit like a prisoner uniform.

explain: 감옥에 있는 사람이 입는 옷이에요. 법에서 쓰는 말은 '수의'인데, '수의'는 죽은 사람에게 입히는 옷도 가리켜서 일상에서는 '죄수복'이 더 편해요. 영화나 분장 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the clothing worn by people in prison. The formal word is '수의', but that sound also means a burial garment, so '죄수복' is easier in daily talk. It often comes up when talking about movies or costumes.

examples.en: After telling a lie, I felt guilty.

examples.ko: 죄악감 때문에 밤에 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I can't sleep at night because of guilt.
He was tormented by guilt for having deceived his friend.

examples.ko: 죄악감을 느낄 필요는 없다고 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: I told her she doesn't need to feel guilty.
It seemed even the guilt was gone, and that scared me.
Guilt shrinks little by little as time passes.

explain: 잘못을 했다는 괴로운 마음을 말해요. 일상에서는 '죄책감'이라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아서, 처음 배울 때는 두 말을 같이 알아 두면 좋아요. '들다, 느끼다, 시달리다'와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is the painful feeling of having done something wrong. In daily life '죄책감' is said far more often, so it helps to learn both together. It often goes with '들다', '느끼다' and '시달리다'.

examples.ko: 이번 사건은 죄질이 아주 나쁘다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the nature of this crime is very bad.
The offense was minor, so he got a fine.
The court viewed the nature of the crime as serious.

examples.ko: 같은 죄라도 죄질에 따라 처벌이 달라져요.
examples.en: Even for the same crime, punishment varies with how bad it is.
The offense was bad, but it was a first offense, so leniency was given.

examples.ko: 죄질까지 따져 보면 결과가 달라질 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you also consider how bad the crime was, the result could change.

explain: 범죄가 얼마나 나쁜지, 어떤 방식으로 저질렀는지를 말할 때 써요. 사람의 성격이 아니라 범행의 내용을 평가하는 말이에요. '죄질이 나쁘다'가 가장 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
explain_en: It is used for how bad a crime is and the way it was committed. It judges the offense itself, not the person's character. '죄질이 나쁘다' is the most common expression.

en: working during the day and studying at night

examples.ko: 그는 낮에는 일하고 밤에는 공부하는 주경야독으로 졸업했어요.
examples.en: He graduated by working by day and studying by night.
After long days of work and nights of study, I finally got the certificate.
Working by day and studying by night is hard but rewarding.
My father is a typical example of working by day and studying by night.

examples.ko: 할머니는 주경야독을 하며 야간 학교를 다니셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother worked by day and went to night school.
Working by day and studying by night is not easy.

explain: 낮에는 일하고 밤에는 공부하며 열심히 사는 모습을 칭찬하는 사자성어예요. 일상에서는 '일하면서 공부하다'라고 많이 말하고, 주경야독은 글이나 이야기에서 감동을 줄 때 잘 나와요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom praises someone who works hard by day and studies at night. In daily speech people say '일하면서 공부하다', while 주경야독 appears in writing or inspiring stories.

examples.ko: 처음 보는 사람들 앞에서 주눅이 들었어요.
examples.en: I felt intimidated in front of people I'd never met.

examples.ko: 발표 때 주눅 들지 말고 자신 있게 말해요.
examples.en: Don't be intimidated during the presentation; speak with confidence.
It seems he lost his nerve because his friend laughed at him.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 주눅 든 목소리로 대답했어요.
examples.en: That child answered in a timid voice.

examples.ko: 너무 주눅 들어 있지 마세요, 괜찮아요.
examples.en: Don't be so timid; it's okay.

examples.ko: 주눅을 풀어 주려고 일부러 농담을 했어요.
examples.en: I joked on purpose to help ease his nervousness.

explain: 거의 '주눅이 들다', '주눅 들다'처럼 써서, 남 앞에서 자신감을 잃고 움츠러드는 모습을 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '기가 죽다'가 있고, 반대 느낌은 '기가 살다'예요.
explain_en: It is used almost only as '주눅이 들다' or '주눅 들다', meaning to lose confidence and shrink back in front of others. A similar expression is '기가 죽다', and the opposite feeling is '기가 살다'.

examples.en: He makes plans very carefully.
He is so meticulous that he almost never makes mistakes.

examples.ko: 팀장님은 정말 주도면밀해서 놓치는 게 없어요.
examples.en: Our team leader is so thorough that nothing gets missed.
The culprit was meticulous but left a small trace.

examples.ko: 이렇게 주도면밀하면 누구라도 믿을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're this thorough, anyone can trust you.
Everyone admired his thoroughness.

explain: '꼼꼼하다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 계획이나 준비에 빈틈이 없다는 뜻으로 써요. 칭찬할 때도 쓰지만 범죄 계획처럼 치밀하게 꾸민 일에도 쓸 수 있어요. 반대말은 '허술하다'예요.
explain_en: It is a more formal word than '꼼꼼하다' and means leaving no gaps in planning or preparation. It can be praise, but it also fits carefully plotted things such as a crime. The opposite is '허술하다'.

examples.en: I prepared the meeting materials meticulously.

examples.ko: 그는 모든 가능성을 주도면밀히 따져 봤어요.
examples.en: He weighed every possibility carefully.
They are investigating the cause of the accident thoroughly.
Even though I checked carefully, an error appeared.

examples.ko: 계획을 주도면밀히 세운 덕분에 일이 잘 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the carefully made plan, things went well.
If you look carefully, you can see even small differences.

explain: 뉴스, 발표, 글에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '꼼꼼히'라고 말해요. '준비하다, 조사하다, 계획하다, 확인하다'와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: This word often appears in news, presentations and writing. In everyday conversation people usually say '꼼꼼히'. It goes well with '준비하다', '조사하다', '계획하다' and '확인하다'.

examples.en: The police are looking for the ringleader of the incident.

examples.ko: 이번 모임의 주동자는 바로 우리 반장이에요.
examples.en: The ringleader of this gathering is our class president.
He was pointed out as the ringleader of the prank.
No one said who the instigator was.
Only the ringleader was punished and the others were forgiven.

examples.ko: 친구들 사이에서 주동자 역할을 하곤 했어요.
examples.en: I used to be the one who led things among my friends.

explain: 소동, 장난, 시위처럼 좋지 않은 일을 앞장서서 이끈 사람에게 주로 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 쓰고 '앞장선 사람'이라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '주모자'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for the person who led a bad event such as a commotion, prank or protest. For good things, people say '앞장선 사람' instead. A similar word is '주모자'.

examples.en: The officiant's speech was so long that the guests got bored.
I cried at my teacher's wedding speech.

examples.ko: 결혼식 때 들은 주례사를 아직도 기억해요.
examples.en: I still remember the speech I heard at the wedding.

examples.ko: 주례사는 보통 짧고 따뜻한 말이 좋아요.
examples.en: A wedding officiant's speech is best when it is short and warm.
In the speech, they said 'respect each other.'
These days many weddings don't have an officiant's speech.

explain: 결혼식에서 주례를 맡은 사람이 신랑 신부에게 해 주는 말이에요. 덕담이 중심이라 '덕담'과 비슷하게 따뜻한 조언이 많아요. 요즘은 주례 없이 하는 결혼식도 있어요.
explain_en: It is what the person officiating a wedding says to the bride and groom. It is mostly good wishes and warm advice, similar to '덕담'. Nowadays some weddings are held without an officiant.

examples.en: Tears streamed down the child's cheeks.
The cup tilted and the water poured out.
Sweat is running down my forehead.
The candle wax melted and ran down.
Raindrops trickle down the window.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보다가 눈물이 주르르 났어요.
examples.en: Tears rolled down while I watched the sad movie.

explain: 눈물, 땀, 빗물이 한 줄기로 길게 흘러내리는 모양을 말해요. '주르륵'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 계속 내리는 비는 '주룩주룩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes tears, sweat or rain running down in a single stream. You can swap it with '주르륵'. Rain that keeps falling is '주룩주룩'.

en: streaming down; spilling out all at once

examples.en: It was slippery, so I slid down the stairs.
Sweat ran down my face.
The soup dripped off the spoon.
Coins spilled out of the pocket.

examples.ko: 눈물이 주르륵 흐르는 걸 참을 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't hold back the tears streaming down.
The ice cream melted and ran down my hand.

explain: 액체뿐 아니라 동전처럼 작은 것이 한꺼번에 흘러내리거나 미끄러지는 모양에도 써요. '주르르'와 비슷해서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 눈물, 땀, 동전, 국물 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: Besides liquids, it also fits small things like coins that spill or slide down all at once. It is close to '주르르', so you can swap them. You often hear it for tears, sweat, coins and soup.

examples.en: That singer dominated the music scene for a long time.
He is someone who once ruled this neighborhood.
Which company dominates the market these days?

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 동네를 주름잡을 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: As a kid I thought I would rule the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 젊은 선수들이 세계 무대를 주름잡고 있어요.
examples.en: Young players are dominating the world stage.
They are the actors who dominated the film world back then.

explain: 어떤 분야나 지역에서 가장 큰 힘과 영향력을 가진다는 뜻이에요. 앞에 '가요계, 시장, 동네'처럼 분야나 장소가 오고 '을/를'을 붙여요. 비슷한 말로 '휩쓸다', '휘어잡다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It means holding the most power and influence in a field or area. A field or place such as '가요계', '시장' or '동네' comes before it with '을/를'. Similar words are '휩쓸다' and '휘어잡다'.

examples.en: I had no time, so I only skimmed through the museum.
If you read in a skimming way, you won't remember the content.

examples.ko: 주마간산처럼 다니면 여행에서 남는 게 없어요.
examples.en: If you travel in a rush, nothing stays with you from the trip.
Don't just glance; look carefully.

examples.ko: 하루에 열 곳을 보는 건 주마간산일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: Seeing ten places in a day is just a quick glance.

examples.ko: 주마간산이라도 한 번 보는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Even a quick look is better than nothing.

explain: 달리는 말 위에서 산을 본다는 뜻에서, 자세히 살피지 않고 대충 지나치는 것을 말해요. 비슷한 표현으로 '수박 겉핥기'가 있어요. 약간 딱딱한 사자성어라 글이나 이야기에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: From the image of looking at mountains from a galloping horse, it means passing by without looking closely. A similar expression is '수박 겉핥기'. It is a somewhat formal idiom, used mainly in writing and storytelling.

examples.ko: 사고 순간 지난 일들이 주마등처럼 스쳐 갔어요.
examples.en: At the moment of the accident, past events flashed through my mind.
Memories like a flickering reel passed through my mind.

examples.ko: 죽기 전에는 주마등이 보인다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: They say a flash of one's whole life appears before death.

examples.ko: 주마등을 보는 것처럼 지난 일 년이 지나갔어요.
examples.en: The past year went by as if I were watching a reel of images.

examples.ko: 졸업식 날 지난 십 년이 주마등같이 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: On graduation day the last ten years flashed back to me.

examples.ko: 주마등 속 장면처럼 어린 시절이 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: My childhood came back like scenes in a flickering reel.

explain: 거의 '주마등처럼 스치다/지나가다' 형태로 쓰여요. 위급한 순간이나 인생을 돌아볼 때, 여러 장면이 빠르게 머릿속을 지나가는 느낌을 말해요.

phrases.example: 눈을 감자 어린 시절이 주마등처럼 스쳐 갔어요.
phrases.en: When I closed my eyes, my childhood flashed through my mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일이나 기억이 아주 빠르게 차례로 떠오를 때 써요. 위급한 순간이나 큰 감정이 있을 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when past events or memories come to mind quickly one after another, often in a crisis or at emotional moments.

explain_en: It is used almost only as '주마등처럼 스치다/지나가다'. It describes many scenes passing quickly through the mind, such as in an emergency or when looking back on life.

examples.en: This is a gift I bought with my own pocket money.
I didn't have enough pocket money, so I couldn't buy a snack.

examples.ko: 형이 주머닛돈을 털어 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: My older brother emptied his own pocket to buy me a meal.

examples.ko: 주머닛돈은 얼마 안 되지만 보태 쓸게요.
examples.en: My own money isn't much, but I'll chip in.

examples.ko: 회삿돈이 아니라 내 주머닛돈이니 아껴야 해요.
examples.en: It's my own money, not the company's, so I have to save.

examples.ko: 주머닛돈 쓰듯이 마음대로 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't spend it freely as if it were your own pocket money.

explain: 공금이나 남의 돈이 아니라 자기가 가진 개인 돈을 말할 때 써요. '내 돈'을 조금 정겹게 말하는 느낌이고, 비슷한 말로 '쌈짓돈'이 있어요. 보통 '주머닛돈으로 사다, 주머닛돈을 털다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means personal money, as opposed to public funds or someone else's money. It sounds like a slightly warm way to say '내 돈', and a similar word is '쌈짓돈'. It is usually used as '주머닛돈으로 사다' or '주머닛돈을 털다'.

examples.ko: 예산을 주먹구구로 짜면 나중에 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you make the budget by rough guesswork, problems will arise later.
This plan is too sloppy.
It's a rough calculation, so it isn't exact.
Don't rely on guesswork; check the numbers.

examples.ko: 주먹구구가 아니라 근거 있는 자료가 필요해요.
examples.en: We need data with evidence, not guesswork.
A rough guess is fine, so please tell me roughly.

explain: 정확하게 따지지 않고 대충 어림으로 계산하거나 일하는 것을 말해요. 보통 안 좋은 뜻으로 쓰고, '대충'보다 일 처리 방식을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. '주먹구구로 하다, 주먹구구가 되다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means calculating or working roughly without checking things properly. It is usually negative and criticizes the way work is done more than '대충' does. It is used as '주먹구구로 하다' or '주먹구구가 되다'.

examples.ko: 주먹구구식 관리 때문에 문제가 계속 생겨요.
examples.en: Problems keep happening because of sloppy management.
I'm worried because the company is run in a slapdash way.
If you do work in a slapdash way, the result is uncertain.
We got away from the sloppy way and made rules.
His rough-and-ready calculations are always wrong.
We have to prepare systematically, not in a slapdash way.

explain: '주먹구구'처럼 대충 어림으로 하는 방식을 가리키며, 체계 없이 하는 일 처리를 비판할 때 써요. 반대는 '체계적'이에요. '-으로'를 붙여 '주먹구구식으로 하다'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Like '주먹구구', it refers to a rough, unsystematic way of doing things and is used to criticize it. The opposite is '체계적'. It is often used with '-으로', as in '주먹구구식으로 하다'.
